title: Challenging an arbitral award - the narrow grounds explained
p1:
Winning an arbitration does not always mean the award is untouchable.

But here is the surprising part: losing a case in arbitration is usually not enough reason to challenge the decision.
p2:
Many people believe an arbitral award can be challenged like a regular court judgment. That is a common misconception.

The law keeps the challenge window narrow. A court generally does not re-hear the entire dispute or decide whether the arbitrator made the “right” decision. It only checks specific issues, such as serious procedural unfairness, violation of legal principles, or grounds that make the award unacceptable under the law.
p3:
The practical takeaway: a challenge is not an appeal in disguise. It is meant to correct fundamental problems, not provide a second chance to argue the same facts.

This limited review protects the speed and finality that make arbitration attractive for businesses and parties.
conclusion: Do you think arbitration should have stricter limits on challenges, or should parties get wider rights to question an award?
